name: Share Links & Access Control
description: Universal access primitive to share galleries, albums, invitations, and downloads securely without requiring end users to create accounts. Supports passwords, expiry, per-action permissions, and optional client identity capture.
goals: A single, consistent mechanism for client access across features.
Fine-grained, auditable policies (view, download, comment, select, RSVP, etc.).
Support link revocation, expiry, and rate limiting to prevent abuse.
Enable link-local language/locale override for client UX.

rules: Share links are workspace-scoped and reference a target resource (gallery_id, album_id, invitation_id, export_id).
Tokens are opaque and non-guessable; storage never exposes sequential IDs.
Policy checks must include workspace_id and target resource state (published, not deleted).

fields.name: token_hash
fields.notes: Store hash of token; never store raw token

workflows.name: Consume Share Link
steps: Client opens share URL containing opaque token.
Frontend exchanges token with validate endpoint to obtain session_token.
If password required, prompt and validate; if identity required, collect minimal fields.
Portal API calls include session_token; backend resolves share_link_id and policy.
Each action checks allowed_actions and logs interaction/audit.

logs: Validation failures with reason (no raw token logged)
traces: Trace validate -> downstream portal request chain
alerts: Excessive validations failures from same IP
High rate of password invalid attempts

controls: Optional password gate stored as hash
Short-lived session tokens for portal actions
Revocation and expiry checks on every request
Public endpoint rate limiting + Turnstile optionally for brute-force protection
privacy: Identity capture is optional and minimal; treat as PII.
Provide workspace setting to anonymize client interactions.

acceptanceTests: Revoked share link blocks access immediately.
Password-protected links require correct password and rate-limit invalid attempts.
Session token cannot be used for a different share link or workspace.
openQuestions: Should share link session tokens be JWTs signed by backend or opaque IDs stored server-side?
Do we support per-link download caps and watermark-only enforcement?
Do we support one-time links (single view) for sensitive deliveries?
